changes.B1: JSONDecoder uses an object_pairs_hook that rejects repeated names before dict construction. Each of the 12 record fields has a same-value duplicate regression; additional records attempt refusal-to-pass and failure-to-pass overwrites.
changes.B2: Both frozen dataclasses require type(protocol) is int and the frozen protocol value. Binding construction, direct record construction and file consumption reject true, 1.0, string 1, and integer 2.
changes.B3: consume_report rejects a binding whose successful-consumption identity is already set before accessing its target. Successful consumption retains the first identity; cleanup does not reset consumption. Invalid reads do not record identity or remove the file.
changes.gaps: Added valid-but-mismatched execution mode/profile, absent target, bad field types (including attempt and bridge exit), exact capacity-exceeded error, correction after invalid reads, and replay/replacement cleanup tests. Corrected the original evidence claims.
changes.test_cleanup: The replacement test retains the original inode by renaming the consumed file instead of unlinking it before replacement, avoiding nondeterministic inode reuse. Existing protocol=2 coverage moved into the protocol matrix instead of remaining duplicated.

negative_contracts.identity: Duplicate names or nonexact protocol types must not become terminal evidence. Run/nonce/attempt/runner/mode/profile must match the binding.
negative_contracts.authorization: Only successful validation grants cleanup authority for the exact file identity. Invalid input and replay cannot grant cleanup authority over a replacement.
negative_contracts.tenancy: Existing checkout/domain path isolation and no-follow helpers remain in force; this repair adds no cross-checkout access path. Same-uid malicious concurrency is outside the verified property.
negative_contracts.input: Duplicate ambiguity, field type coercion, malformed payloads and excessive bytes must be rejected; the size error is specifically capacity-exceeded.
negative_contracts.state: A binding is single-use after successful consumption, including after cleanup; an invalid first read leaves it usable for corrected input.
negative_contracts.exposure: Existing fixed report errors and private field allowlist remain; exact absent/oversized error messages are asserted without paths or input contents.
negative_contracts.availability: Existing REPORT_MAX_BYTES+1 bounded read is retained; oversized input is rejected before JSON parsing.
negative_contracts.dependencies: Only the stdlib JSON decoder and existing private-file helpers are involved. No dependency, subprocess, native bridge or public schema changes.

test_environment.mode: Frozen ptest dispatcher, local backend, one worker; controller virtualenv with this worktree's source and tests. No worktree virtualenv was created or shared.

Other reported integration cases were below 0.2s. No new sleeps or slow tests were added.

dan_three_passes.pass_1_re_read: Re-read the production and abuse-test changes against the initial full-file read. The duplicate hook rejects names before dict collapse; exact protocol checks cover both constructors; the consumed identity is set only after decoding succeeds and is not reset by cleanup.
dan_three_passes.pass_2_source_of_truth: Compared the repair and original foundation briefs, Opus B1/B2/B3 and notes, design report bounds/identity/native-scope constraints, existing private-file helpers and callers. Verified through real files that invalid reads retain the target, replay cannot overwrite cleanup identity, and restoring the first file still permits cleanup.
dan_three_passes.pass_3_smell_sweep: Searched report/binding/consumer symbols. There are no production consumers outside this foundation yet. The existing consumed identity also represents the spent state, avoiding a second mutable flag or global replay registry. Preserved existing no-follow/path/byte bounds and kept CLI, adapters, native execution and public schemas unchanged. Improved the existing inode replacement fixture and removed overlapping protocol=2 test coverage.

security_gates.not_run: Bandit, Gitleaks, dependency-advisory and property/fuzz scanners are not configured in this slice. No .github workflow exists here; pyproject and scripts expose no scanner gate. The design's broader security/release gates remain separate work; none is claimed passed.

not_verified: Native CLI execution and report production/operations wiring
Real foreign-owner fixtures or concurrent hostile replacement during the lstat/read/unlink windows
Concurrent consumes of the same binding or replay through a reconstructed/copied binding; the repaired contract is sequential consumption of the executor-owned binding

residual_risks: The pre-existing shared read helper does not compare its opened descriptor identity with the before/after lstat identities; same-uid replacement during that window remains outside this repair.
Cleanup still has the pre-existing lstat-to-unlink race; deterministic replacement before cleanup is covered, not an atomic unlink identity guarantee.
